extracted.intended_audience: senior/key personnel and other significant contributors preparing NIH biographical sketches for grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and required content/format for the NIH biographical sketch (PHS/OMB form) for senior/key personnel and other significant contributors in grant applications, including Personal Statement, Positions, Contributions to Science, Education/Training, and selected publications. Emphasizes following the provided format and page limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the specified section headings and ordering for each person; ensure the entire biographical sketch content for an individual does not exceed five pages. Examples in the document adhere to this structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required identifying information
rubrics_metrics.description: NAME; eRA COMMONS USER NAME (credential, e.g., agency login); POSITION TITLE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the person's full name, eRA Commons username (or other credential), and current position title at the top of the biosketch for each senior/key personnel or contributor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education/Training table
rubrics_metrics.description: EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, include postdoctoral training and residency training if applicable. Add/delete rows as necessary.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rows with INSTITUTION AND LOCATION, DEGREE (if applicable), Completion Date MM/YYYY, and FIELD OF STUDY. Begin with baccalaureate and include subsequent professional, residency, and postdoctoral training as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Personal Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal Statement section describing the individual's qualifications, relevant experience, and role for the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the candidate's background, summary of relevant accomplishments (e.g., publication counts, prior collaborations), specific expertise and what they will contribute to the proposed grant (e.g., develop analysis plans, provide expertise on data quality). Use concise narrative to link past work to the proposed role; examples in the document show tailored statements referencing specific skills and planned contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Positions, Scientific Appointments, and Honors
rubrics_metrics.description: List positions and scientific appointments with dates, plus professional honors and memberships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide chronological entries for academic/clinical/research positions, leadership roles, and selected honors. Include membership in professional societies and notable awards. Use dates and institution/organization identifiers (examples: 'Associate Professor, Vanderbilt University Medical Center, 2015 -').

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Contributions to Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the individual's major scientific contributions with narrative descriptions and representative citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numbered contribution items summarizing distinct research themes or methodological advances, each followed by 1–4 representative citations (full citations as shown). Include brief statements of significance/impact and how the work advances the field. Examples on the page show substantive narratives (e.g., Bayesian latent variable models) followed by citations labeled a., b., c., etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications directly relevant to the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: List publications directly relevant to the proposed work under the individual's biosketch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and list key, directly relevant peer-reviewed publications (full citations). The document also provides a link to the 'Complete List of Published Work in MyBibliography' — include or reference the full bibliography if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing and recently completed projects / grant roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Report ongoing and recently completed projects (grant titles, grant numbers, funding agency), the individual's role, and project dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each project include the project title, grant identifier (e.g., R01 AI139172), sponsor (e.g., NIH/NIAID), brief project goal, role (e.g., Principal Investigator, Co-Investigator), and start/end dates. Examples on the page list multiple projects with roles and timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide representative evidence of expertise (examples and citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use representative publications and project descriptions as evidence of expertise and relevance to the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific peer-reviewed articles, clinical trials, methodological papers, and other outputs that support claims made in the Personal Statement and Contributions to Science sections. The biosketch examples include explicit citations (with PMIDs/PMCID when available) to substantiate described contributions.
